(kam) here is khabariyyah (a declarative "how many") indicating abundance: meaning, "How many a generation have We destroyed before them" ﴿before them﴾ [Qaf: 36], i.e., before your people, Quraysh, ﴿generations﴾ [Qaf: 36], meaning groups who lived in a limited period, which they estimated at one hundred years.

The word qarn may carry a broader meaning than this when it is linked to a prophet, such as the people of Nuh (peace be upon him), who were all united (iqtaranu) in his prophethood, which lasted nine hundred and fifty years. Thus qarn derives from iqtiran (conjunction), whether that conjunction is in the time of a king, a prophet, or an event.

In another verse, the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, explained how He destroyed the nations that denied before them, saying, glorified is He: ﴿So each one We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those who were seized by the Cry, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 40].

All of these were stronger than Quraysh in power and might. And where are they from Iram of the pillars, the like of which was never created in the lands? And where are they from Pharaoh of the stakes?

﴿So they explored through the lands﴾ [Qaf: 36]: they moved about in them and traveled through them, and moving about is a sign of strength and power, and that they were not preoccupied with the affairs of their livelihood.

The Truth, glorified is He, has also made clear that movement and travel on the earth may be for reflection, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see﴾ [An-Naml: 69], and it may be for seeking provision and tourism, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then observe﴾ [Al-An'am: 11].

So: ﴿they explored through the lands﴾ [Qaf: 36], they traveled through them for enjoyment and benefit, for they were not content with what was in their own homelands, but traversed other lands. Such conduct belongs only to the strong; as for the weak, he does not leave his place and is content with little.

In another place He said of them: ﴿They tilled the earth and developed it more than they developed it﴾ [Ar-Rum: 9].

The word naqaba indicates searching for what is not apparent, for what is hidden within the earth. So: they were not content with the apparent blessings, but sought out what was hidden of them.

His saying: ﴿Is there any escape?﴾ [Qaf: 36], i.e., a refuge to which they might resort and which would protect them from the punishment. The meaning is that these people, despite their power, establishment, and roaming across the expanses of the earth, when the punishment descended upon them, did not find any refuge to protect them, nor any shelter to repel the punishment of Allah from them.

The word ﴿maḥīṣ﴾ [Qaf: 36] derives from ḥāṣa, so the one who does it is ḥāyiṣ. We say it even in colloquial speech, meaning: a bewildered person who goes here and goes there, and no one comes to his aid, so there is no escape and no flight.

The intended meaning has been expressed in the interrogative form ﴿Is there any escape?﴾ [Qaf: 36], so that you would answer and acknowledge the reality: Did they find a refuge to which they could resort from the punishment? The answer is no.

This verse was revealed to console our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to lighten his burden because of the hardship and obstinacy he faced from his people, as if the Exalted were saying to His Prophet: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, and take as an example your brothers among the earlier messengers; victory will be yours in the end.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 50, verse 37:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, in that⁠—﴾ [Qaf: 37] means: in the accounts of the earlier nations whom Allah seized. ﴿Surely there is a reminder⁠—﴾ [Qaf: 37] a reminder to you, one that required you to take warning from them, and their news has reached you, either by witnessing their traces and the remains of their dwellings: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138].

Or their news reached you by hearing it from the heavenly scriptures. Hearing and sight are the most important means of perception in a human being. Therefore He said here: ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf: 37], meaning: he listens and he witnesses.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿for whoever has a heart⁠—﴾ [Qaf: 37] means: a heart that is aware, reflective and perceptive, not heedless or negligent. Otherwise, what is the benefit of hearing for one who does not have this heart? He hears from here and it goes out from here, so he gains nothing from what he hears.

The phrase ﴿or gives ear⁠—﴾ [Qaf: 37] contains a metonymy for giving attention to what is heard. He did not say, for example, of one who hears, "He merely lends his ear and listens," but rather "he gives ear" with a present heart, so that he comprehends what is heard and receives it with the appropriate rational inquiry.

﴿while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf: 37]. "Shahid" (witness) is an intensive form on the pattern fa'il, which also indicates attention to what he observes and benefit from it. He hears and observes with a present heart and an aware understanding, far from heedlessness.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We certainly created the heavens and the earth...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 50, verse 38:

The Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear to us that He created the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them of cosmic signs, within a total of six days. ﴿And We did not feel any fatigue from creating them﴾ [Qaf: 38]: no weariness or exhaustion afflicted us.

This verse has parallels in the Noble Qur'an which indicate that the days of creation were eight days. Read: ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and set up for Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Fussilat: 9]. So we now have two days. ﴿And He placed firm mountains upon it from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 10]. Thus the total becomes six days. ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens in two days..﴾ [Fussilat: 11-12].

So the apparent total is eight days, and this led some orientalists to accuse the verses of contradiction, asking whether it is six days or eight. This accusation arises from their failure to understand the methods and purposes of the language.

The Truth, glory be to Him, first spoke of the creation of the earth as an independent body, then He spoke of the creation of what follows the earth within a complete four days. Thus the time frame here overlaps, and the first two days are included in the completion of the four, because they concern the creation of one thing, which is the earth.

Therefore, after speaking of the creation of the earth, He said, glory be to Him: ﴿in four days, alike for those who ask﴾ [Fussilat: 10], meaning: the completion of the four days was equal (for all who ask). It is like saying: "We travelled from Cairo to Tanta in one hour, and to Alexandria in two hours." So there is no contradiction in the verses; rather they are in harmony with one another.

Among the issues they raised about this verse is their claim: if the Truth, glory be to Him, executes His will and does not need to labour in the act, then why did He not create this universe with the word "Be" (kun), without the creation taking six days?

In explaining this, we said that there is a difference between creating a thing and setting up the preconditions for its creation; then the thing itself turns and interacts until it becomes what it becomes.

We illustrated this by making a yoghurt pot: we take milk and starter culture and mix them, then place this mixture at a certain temperature, and after a period these components interact and give us yoghurt.

So: this matter took a few minutes to prepare, but it interacted over several hours until it became what we want, after we put in it the origins and materials that constitute it. Likewise in the matter of the creation of the universe in six days, of course of the days we know.

The meaning of *lughub* (fatigue, lassitude) is the weakness that comes after the exhaustion of work. So *nasab* (toil) and *ta'ab* (weariness) accompany work, while *lughub* is weakness and slackening after completion. When the lesser is negated, the greater is negated all the more by way of priority: it did not happen.

So the meaning is that neither weakness nor weariness befell Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep seizes Him..﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. *Sinah* is a drowsiness that precedes sleep, so negating drowsiness means negating sleep all the more by way of priority.

Al-Sha'rawi's Commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 50, verses 39–40:

Allah the Exalted wishes to console His Messenger (ﷺ) after what he suffered from the harm of his people. He tells him: proceed with the matter of your call, do not grieve over what they say, and do not despair of your victory over them, for when the Messenger of Allah and his Companions were pressed hard by harm, they were slow to expect victory.

In this regard Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. Here He says to him: ﴿So be patient...﴾ [Qaf: 39], because every patience upon trial and harm is rewarded with merit and rank. Whenever they increase in harm, be patient with their harm: they increase in sin, and you increase in reward.

As for His saying: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord...﴾ [Qaf: 39], meaning: declare your Lord free of every deficiency and of everything unbefitting Him of the attributes that His creation possesses. Allah has a hand, but not like our hands, and He has hearing, but not like our hearing. So take these attributes within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

Therefore Allah the Exalted began the report of the Night Journey and the Ascension with His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night...﴾ [al-Isra': 1], meaning: He exalts Allah above the attributes of deficiency and above resemblance to His creation, because in the story there is a breach of the laws that creatures know.

So do not deem this event improbable, since it is ascribed to Allah, not to human beings. Muhammad did not say "I traveled" but rather said: "I was taken by night" (usriya bi).

Speed in covering a distance is measured by the power of the agent. You travel from Cairo to Alexandria by horse in ten hours, by car in three hours, by airplane in half an hour, and by rocket in a few minutes.

Thus speed is proportionate to its agent: whenever power increases, time decreases. If the one who possesses the speed is Allah the Exalted, then time is not mentioned here, and that the Messenger of Allah spent a night on this journey is because he was shown several signs which took up this time.

The meaning of ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord﴾ [Qaf: 39] is: glorify your Lord with glorification joined to praise for His blessings. Therefore you find that the word tasbih (glorification) always comes joined with one of Allah's blessings, and a sign that none other than Him can accomplish: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night...﴾ [al-Isra': 1], ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36].

Therefore, throughout history we have seen disbelievers, polytheists and atheists worship their idols and gods and sanctify them, yet no one has said to his object of worship "Subhanaka" (Glory be to You) forever, because it is said only to Allah.

Likewise, no one has named anyone with the name Allah, despite the presence of atheists and deniers of divinity; yet none of them has dared to name his son by this name, for he fears to name his son Allah.

Therefore Allah said: ﴿Do you know anyone worthy of His name?﴾ [Maryam: 65]. So these are two matters that no one has dared to do, out of the greatness of Allah the Exalted, even in matters where creatures have choice.

As we understand from His saying ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord...﴾ [Qaf: 39], this glorification is one of the blessings that require praise. That the Exalted Truth is free of likeness, free of equal, free of partner, is among the greatest blessings upon the servants.

For if Allah had an equal, a partner or a peer, our lives would be corrupted, we would be wretched through that likeness, and life would not be pleasant for us.

Therefore He says: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22], and He said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

The meaning of ﴿Before the rising of the sun and before setting, and from the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 39–40] is: glorify Him with a glorification that is continuous and never ceases. These mentioned times encompass the day and the night, for among people are those who work by day and sleep by night, and among them are those who work by night and sleep by day; the obligation of the one has ended by night, and the obligation of the other has ended by day.

This verse has counterparts in other verses, but each has its own meaning. Allah says in another place: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. Here He said ﴿al-ghurub﴾ (the setting) [Qaf: 39], and there He said ﴿ghurubiha﴾ (its setting) [Ta-Ha: 130]. They asked: what is the difference between them, and which of them is more eloquent?

We say: each word is eloquent in its place. When the sun sets, some of us witness the sign of sunset, and some of us do not witness it due to cloud or other things, and judge by the setting from other indications that point to it.

Therefore in Ramadan, for example, many of us do not see the sunset, yet they break their fast because they have other evidence of the time. So His saying ﴿and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130] is for one who witnesses the setting, and His saying ﴿before the setting﴾ [Qaf: 39] is for one who does not witness it.

Likewise, in His saying: ﴿And from the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], and He said in another place: ﴿And from the hours of the night, glorify...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. The first is for one who wishes to glorify at one time of the night and then sleep, and the second is for one who wishes to glorify, then sleep, then glorify again, then sleep, meaning several times during the night.

The meaning of ﴿and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40] is: after the prayers, and our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), explained to us how to glorify after the prayers.

The meaning of ﴿Before the rising of the sun and before setting, and from the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 39–40] is: glorify Him with a glorification that is continuous and never ceases. These mentioned times encompass the day and the night, for among people are those who work by day and sleep by night, and among them are those who work by night and sleep by day; the obligation of the one has ended by night, and the obligation of the other has ended by day.

This verse has counterparts in other verses, but each has its own meaning. Allah says in another place: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. Here He said ﴿al-ghurub﴾ (the setting) [Qaf: 39], and there He said ﴿ghurubiha﴾ (its setting) [Ta-Ha: 130]. They asked: what is the difference between them, and which of them is more eloquent?

We say: each word is eloquent in its place. When the sun sets, some of us witness the sign of sunset, and some of us do not witness it due to cloud or other things, and judge by the setting from other indications that point to it.

Therefore in Ramadan, for example, many of us do not see the sunset, yet they break their fast because they have other evidence of the time. So His saying ﴿and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130] is for one who witnesses the setting, and His saying ﴿before the setting﴾ [Qaf: 39] is for one who does not witness it.

Likewise, in His saying: ﴿And from the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], and He said in another place: ﴿And from the hours of the night, glorify...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. The first is for one who wishes to glorify at one time of the night and then sleep, and the second is for one who wishes to glorify, then sleep, then glorify again, then sleep, meaning several times during the night.

The meaning of ﴿and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40] is: after the prayers, and our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), explained to us how to glorify after the prayers.

The caller here is Israfil, the angel charged with blowing the Trumpet, and the "Cry" (al-sayha) meant is the second blast, which brings people out of their graves for resurrection. Allah, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And listen, on the day the Caller calls from a near place﴾ [Qaf: 41].

This speech comes after what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ suffered of harm, by word and by deed. It is as if his Lord, mighty and majestic, is consoling him, saying to him: If they have done that, then wait for this day, the day the Caller calls out to them, the day they stand for reckoning and recompense.

And listen to what happens among them in this situation, how they will regret, how some of them will disown others, curse one another and revile one another, as they say in the peasant proverb (bukra n'a'ud 'ala al-hitta wa nisma' al-zitta): meaning, wait, O Muhammad, and you will hear about them.

As for His saying ﴿from a near place﴾ [Qaf: 41], it means that the Caller will be near to each one, as if he were attached to him, and as if each one of us had with him his caller.

﴿The day they hear the Cry in truth﴾ [Qaf: 42], that is, the second blast,
﴿in truth﴾ [Qaf: 42], the truth which they used to deny in the world and disbelieve in, which is the resurrection.

The Qur'an has related their saying: ﴿When we are dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 5]. And His saying, glorified be He: ﴿That is the Day of Emergence﴾ [Qaf: 42], that is, the resurrection and the coming out of the graves. The second blast will come after all creatures have died by the first blast.

Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah, would always recite Surah Qaf on the two Eids, because of the saying of the Exalted within it: ﴿That is the Day of Emergence﴾ [Qaf: 42]. Going out is recommended on the two Eids, even the menstruating woman goes out, not for prayer, but to witness the good and the congregation of the Muslims on this day.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah prescribed that the Eid prayer be held in the open field (al-khala'), because it is a prayer attended by those whose prayer would not be valid for them.

Also, reciting Surah Qaf on the two Eids is a reminder that the day of Eid, the going out, the joy and the adornment should not make us forget the greatest Day of Emergence, the Day of Resurrection.

After Allah, glory be to Him, said ﴿That is the Day of Coming Forth﴾ [Qaf: 42], He establishes this reality and brings the conclusion, saying ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death...﴾ [Qaf: 43]. And because some deny this reality, He affirmed it by repeating the pronoun.

﴿Indeed, it is We...﴾ [Qaf: 43]: He alone, glory be to Him, is capable of that. ﴿And to Us is the final return﴾ [Qaf: 43], i.e., the place of return and the ultimate destination. So the beginning is from Us and the end is to Us.

﴿On the Day the earth will split open from them, hastening...﴾ [Qaf: 44], i.e., they will come out of it hurrying, because they respond to the Blast at one and the same time, so they come out hastening without delay.

﴿That...﴾ [Qaf: 44] refers to what happens on that Day: the splitting of the earth, the people coming out of their graves hastening, and their gathering in one place for the Gathering (al-hashr). ﴿And that is easy for Us﴾ [Qaf: 44].

Since We know best what they say, leave the requital to Us. For if you were to requite them, you would requite them according to your strength, whereas We requite them according to Our strength. We will not show them mercy, and they will not escape punishment. So leave this matter to Us, for We are more capable of disciplining them.

﴿And you are not over them a compeller.﴾ [Qaf: 45] Your mission is only to convey the message, so do not exhaust yourself on their account, and do not burden yourself beyond its capacity, just as the Truth, glorified is He, rebuked him in His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3]

The meaning of ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾ [Qaf: 45] is: you are not to compel them to faith, for if I had willed that, I would have compelled them to faith as I compelled others. Rather, I want them to come willingly, choosing freely.

﴿So remind by the Qur'an﴾ [Qaf: 45] — this is your mission: to remind people by this Qur'an.

Then He restricted the reminding here by His saying: ﴿him who fears My warning﴾ [Qaf: 45], that is, who fears My threat and My warning. None fears the warning except a believer who has readiness and capacity to receive and respond.

We have already explained the difference between the agent and that which is capable of being acted upon. Not everyone who hears the Qur'an is alike. Among people is one who listens and the hearing bears fruit in him, so he responds, and among them is one who listens without awareness and without reflection, so it is as if he had heard nothing.

Therefore the Almighty said, describing them: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad: 16].

This listening is the work of the limbs alone, without a heart that receives and comprehends. ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; but those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them.﴾ [Fussilat: 44]

So the Qur'an is one, but the receptacle differs. Among people is one who listens with an attentive heart, a pure soul, and a mind free of opposites and corrupt creeds, so he is affected and responds; and among them is one who listens with a stubborn heart and a mind occupied with contrary creeds that prevent him from responding.

Therefore, we have said to one who weighs two matters: you should remove everyone from your heart, then empty yourself of yourself, and reflect and investigate the two matters.

The Almighty said: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up before God, in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾ [Saba': 46].

Collective thinking is disorganized and generally does not arrive at the right answer.

You will recall that we said, in clarifying the differing effect of one and the same act, that you blow on your hands in winter to warm them, and you blow on tea, for instance, to cool it.

Here the Almighty specified the reminding to ﴿him who fears My warning﴾ [Qaf: 45], because he is the one with an attentive heart and a mind free of opposition, free of deceit and of error. This is the proper receptivity to the Qur'an.
